<b>Длительный голод.</b> Мозг перестраив: Prolonged starvation. The brain adapts and covers up to 2/3 of its needs with ketone bodies — glucose use, and with it protein breakdown, drops sharply: the body spares protein. The kidneys also make glucose. Fat lasts 1–2 months (in a person of normal weight); death comes when vital proteins start to be broken down.
<b>Транскрипция</b> — переписывание гена: Transcription is the copying of a gene from DNA into RNA in the nucleus. RNA polymerase II (orange, atomic structure PDB 5FLM), together with transcription factors, binds to the promoter (yellow zone, TATA box), unwinds about 14 base pairs and moves along the template strand 3′→5′, building RNA 5′→3′ by complementary base pairing (U instead of T). Above is the real structure of the yeast regulatory protein GAL4 on its DNA site (PDB 1D66): this is how activators recognize their target genes by the sequence in the major groove. While the RNA is still being made, a cap (purple) is added to its 5′ end. After passing the polyadenylation signal, the polymerase cuts the RNA and leaves the DNA.
<b>Созревание (процессинг) мРНК</b> у эу: mRNA maturation (processing) in eukaryotes. The gene is split: coding exons (colored) alternate with introns (gray). The spliceosome (made of small nuclear RNAs and proteins) cuts out the introns as a “lariat” loop and joins the exons; in this way different mRNAs can be assembled from a single gene (alternative splicing). The 5′ end already carries a cap (7-methylguanosine, lilac; added during synthesis), and a poly-A tail is added at the 3′ end (red) of 100–250 adenylate residues to the 3′ end. The excised lariats are degraded, and the mature mRNA leaves through a nuclear pore into the cytoplasm.
<b>Трансляция</b> на рибосоме. Модель —: Translation on the ribosome. The model is a real bacterial 70S ribosome (eukaryotes have 80S; same principle) with mRNA and three tRNAs (PDB 1VY4): on top the 50S large subunit (rRNA — light-blue strands, proteins — blue), below the small 30S subunit (rRNA — golden, proteins — orange). mRNA is read in codons of 3 nucleotides starting from AUG (methionine). tRNAs (L-shaped, anticodon loop in pink) bring amino acids: the anticodon pairs with the codon in the A site, the ribosome (its rRNA is a ribozyme) transfers the growing chain from the P site onto the new amino acid and moves along by one codon, and the empty tRNA leaves through the E site. At the stop codon (UAA) the protein is released. Turn on an antibiotic.
\n <div><h2>Генетический код</h2>\n:
The genetic code

The code is triplet (a codon is 3 nucleotides), degenerate (61 sense codons for 20 amino acids), unambiguous, non-overlapping, comma-free and almost universal across all living things. AUG is the start codon (methionine); UAA, UAG and UGA are stop codons.

The cost of a protein

Loading an amino acid onto its tRNA by aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase costs 2 high-energy bonds (ATP → AMP); entry of the tRNA into the A site and translocation cost one GTP each — about 4 high-energy bonds per peptide bond.

After translation

Proteins fold (often with the help of chaperones), are cleaved (proinsulin → insulin), phosphorylated and glycosylated, and acquire prosthetic groups and targeting signals. Gene expression is regulated at the level of transcription (operons in bacteria, transcription factors and enhancers in eukaryotes), processing, mRNA stability and translation.

\n <div><h2>Ферменты</h2>\n:
Enzymes

Enzymes are biological catalysts made of protein. Three properties set them apart from other catalysts: enormous efficiency, strict specificity and the capacity for regulation.

Simple enzymes consist of protein only (pepsin, amylase, lipase). Conjugated enzymes consist of a protein part (the apoenzyme) and a non-protein cofactor: either tightly bound — a prosthetic group (metal ions, heme) — or an easily detached coenzyme (most often a vitamin derivative). Together they form the holoenzyme.

How an enzyme speeds up a reaction

An enzyme does not change the energy of the starting materials or products, but it lowers the activation energy — the barrier that must be overcome (graph on the right). Mechanisms: precise orientation of the substrate (binding at a minimum of three points), strain on its bonds, acid–base catalysis (like Glu35 and Asp52 of lysozyme, or the histidine of many enzymes) and covalent catalysis.

Michaelis–Menten stages: E + S ⇄ ES → ES* → EP → E + P.

Specificity

  • Absolute — a single substrate (arginase → arginine only).
  • Relative — a group of similar substrates (lipase — all fats, pepsin — proteins).
  • Stereospecificity — only one isomer (L- or D-).
  • Reaction specificity: from histidine, histidase makes a keto acid, while a decarboxylase makes histamine.

<b>β-Окисление в митохондрии.</b> Жирная: β-Oxidation in the mitochondrion. The fatty acid is first activated in the cytoplasm (acyl-CoA, at the cost of ATP). The inner mitochondrial membrane is impermeable to acyl-CoA, so it is carried across by carnitine (the shuttle: carnitine acyltransferase I, translocase, carnitine acyltransferase II — lilac). In the matrix a cycle of 4 reactions repeats: oxidation (FAD) → hydration → oxidation (NAD⁺) → thiolysis. Each turn cuts 2 carbons off the chain as acetyl-CoA and yields FADH₂ and NADH. Palmitate (C16) goes through 7 turns and gives 8 acetyl-CoA. Fat oxidation also produces “metabolic water” (about 1 g of water per 1 g of fat) — desert rodents, for example, depend on it.
<b>Гипоталамус</b> — нижняя часть промеж: The hypothalamus is the lower part of the diencephalon, with more than 30 pairs of nuclei. It holds the centers of hunger and thirst, sexual and parental behavior, fear and aggression, sleep and the biological clock. Together with the pituitary gland it controls many endocrine glands: the posterior lobe releases hormones made in hypothalamic neurons, and the anterior lobe obeys the hypothalamus’s releasing and inhibiting hormones (liberins and statins). Try the experiments.
\n <div><h2>Как устроено зрение</h2:
How vision works

Optics. Light is refracted by the cornea (about 43 diopters) and the lens (about 19 at rest). The retina receives a reduced, inverted image. To look at something close, the ciliary muscle contracts, the zonular fibers slacken and the lens becomes more convex: this is accommodation.

Retina. About 120 million rods (twilight vision) and about 6 million cones (color and detail). Retinal neurons compress their signals, and roughly 1 million optic nerve fibers carry them to the brain.

The chiasm

In the chiasm, fibers from the nasal halves of the retinas cross to the opposite side, while fibers from the temporal halves continue straight on. That is why the right hemisphere receives the left half of the visual field from both eyes, and the left hemisphere receives the right half. The colors show it: turquoise fibers carry the left field, lilac fibers the right.

Further on

The optic tract ends in the lateral geniculate body of the thalamus. From there the optic radiation curves around the lateral ventricle and reaches the primary visual cortex (V1) of the occipital lobe, along the banks of the calcarine sulcus. Every point of the visual field has its own place in the cortex.

What is accurate here

  • The course of the four fiber bundles and the visual field defects caused by damage to the optic nerve, chiasm and tract.
  • The direction of the focusing error in myopia, hyperopia and presbyopia.

Simplifications

  • Rays inside the eye are drawn schematically, without an exact calculation of refraction.
  • The position of the geniculate body is labeled approximately.
  • The signal wave is greatly slowed down.

The peripheral branch runs to the skin and senses touch, the central branch goes into the CNS. In fast touch fibers both branches are myelinated, and the signal bypasses the cell body. Motor memory is stored at the synapses of this tree. Turn the scene sideways, and the tree becomes a thin strip.
\n <div><h2>Как устроен нейрон</h2>:
How a neuron is built

A neuron has a cell body (soma) with a nucleus and ribosomes, where proteins are synthesized, and two kinds of processes. Dendrites receive signals and carry them to the cell body. The cell body sums excitatory and inhibitory inputs and decides whether to fire a response. The axon carries the impulse away to other cells. The axon leaves the cell body at a site called the axon hillock.

Dendrite and axon

A dendrite is shorter (about 0.5–1 mm), branches at acute angles and tapers like a tree branch. An axon is from centimeters to a meter or more long. It keeps a constant diameter of 0.5–1.5 µm and branches at right angles: collaterals copy the signal to several targets. Dendrites in the CNS are usually unmyelinated, axons are often myelinated. Nissl substance is present in dendrites but absent from the axon.

Three functional classes

Sensory (afferent) neurons sit at the input, interneurons link input to output, and in a complex nervous system they are the most numerous. Effector (efferent) neurons sit at the output: motor neurons control muscles, autonomic neurons control organs.

How cells were first seen

In 1837 Purkinje fixed the soft tissue of the cerebellum and made out large cells. Golgi invented silver staining, Ramón y Cajal drew the finest branchings and synapses, and both received the 1906 Nobel Prize. Nissl stained ribosomes with methylene blue.

What is accurate here

  • The number and arrangement of processes in each shape.
  • Acute branching angles in dendrites, right angles in axon collaterals.
  • The flat tree of the Purkinje cell, the spines of the pyramidal neuron, the T-shaped process of the sensory neuron.
  • The look of the stains: a black silhouette on orange, Nissl substance only in the cell body and dendrite bases.

Simplifications

  • Cell sizes are equalized, and axons are greatly shortened.
  • The impulse is slowed roughly a thousandfold.
  • The Golgi method stains only some cells; here all of them are stained.

<b>Мозг тормозит рефлекс.</b> На вставоч: The brain inhibits the reflex. Axons from the brain (blue signal from above) reach the interneuron of the intermediate zone. If the brain manages to send an inhibitory signal in time, the hand is not pulled away: this is how we hold still while blood is taken from a finger. <b>Мембранный рецептор и цАМФ.</b> Адрен: Membrane receptor and cAMP. Epinephrine does not enter the cell. It binds to the β2-adrenergic receptor (orange, seven helices in the membrane) — this is the real structure of the receptor in complex with a G protein (PDB 3SN6, Nobel Prize 2012). The receptor changes shape, the G protein α subunit (Gαs, light blue) exchanges GDP for GTP, separates from βγ and switches on adenylyl cyclase (green, cryo-EM structure 6R3Q): ATP is turned into molecules of cAMP, the second messenger. cAMP pulls off the regulatory subunits of protein kinase A, and the freed catalytic subunits (pink) phosphorylate phosphorylase kinase → glycogen phosphorylase → glucose 1-phosphate pours out of glycogen. Each step amplifies the signal: one hormone molecule yields millions of glucose molecules. Phosphodiesterase (gray) destroys cAMP and switches the signal off.
\n <div><h2>Два пути сигнала</h2>\n:
Two signaling routes

Hydrophilic hormones (proteins, peptides, catecholamines) act through membrane receptors: ionotropic (channels), metabotropic (via G proteins: Gs activates adenylyl cyclase, Gi inhibits it, Gq activates phospholipase C → IP₃ and Ca²⁺ + DAG), and enzyme receptors (tyrosine kinases, guanylyl cyclase). Second messengers: cAMP, cGMP, Ca²⁺, IP₃, DAG, NO. The response takes seconds to minutes and changes enzyme activity.

Lipophilic hormones (steroids, iodothyronines, calcitriol) enter the cell and act on genes through intracellular receptors: the response takes hours and changes the amount of enzymes.

Hierarchy

Hypothalamus (releasing and inhibiting hormones) → pituitary (tropic hormones: ACTH, TSH, FSH, LH, GH, prolactin) → peripheral glands. Negative feedback: the hormones of the glands inhibit the hypothalamus and pituitary.
